title_original: Steven Spielberg to make a western written by Paul Thomas Anderson
excerpt_original: Jessie Buckley, Cillian Murphy and Mark Rylance will reportedly star in adaptation of The Heart in Winter Steven Spielberg has announced his next project: a western scripted by Paul Thomas Anderson. According to Deadline , the two Oscar-winning film-makers will collaborate for…

blocks.text: Steven Spielberg has announced his next project: a western scripted by Paul Thomas Anderson .
According to Deadline , the two Oscar-winning film-makers will collaborate for an adaptation of Kevin Barry’s 2024 novel The Heart in Winter.
The film is set to bring together the Oscar-winning actors Jessie Buckley, Cillian Murphy and Mark Rylance. It tells the story of two fugitives on the run in the 1890s.

“It’s really the excitement for me to get to work together with my dear friend and colleague Paul Thomas Anderson on a genre, but more particularly, the genre notwithstanding, a story that quite quickly became close to both our hearts and we felt that we could do as a team,” Spielberg told Deadline.

Earlier this year, Spielberg also spoke about the film while at SXSW. “Can’t reveal anything right now, but I have a western in development,” he said, before adding that “it kicks ass” and “there will be no tropes”.

It will be the first time Anderson will have written a complete script for a different director, although he was involved in uncredited rewrites of Martin Scorsese’s Killers of the Flower Moon and Ridley Scott’s Napoleon. He recently won three Oscars for One Battle After Another.
The Guardian’s Sandra Newman called The Heart in Winter one of the best books of 2024, writing that it “effortlessly walks the line between goofy and gothic”.

“This story is about the people who refused to settle for a life that is less than they deserve but maybe more than they can handle,” Spielberg also added. “Jessie and Cillian were the first people to ever come to mind for this and they also have never made a film together.”

Earlier this year, Buckley won the best actress Oscar for her performance in Hamnet, produced by Spielberg, and will next be seen in The Three Incestuous Sisters alongside Saoirse Ronan, Dakota Johnson and Josh O’Connor.

Murphy, who won the best actor Oscar for Oppenheimer, was last seen reprising his role of Jim in 28 Years Later: The Bone Temple and in Peaky Blinders: The Immortal Man. Next summer will also see him return to the Quiet Place franchise.
The film will follow Spielberg’s sci-fi thriller Disclosure Day which made $247m worldwide upon release this past summer.
A release date is yet to be officially confirmed yet but the film is believed to be scheduled for 2028.
